content:
james: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression in kernel selection for long sequences (>1k). latency jumps ~20% on rtx-a100 workloads. suspect register spilling + smem bank conflicts when we take the 'seqlen-optimized' path.

anita: repro? can you paste the exact config + trace?

james: repro script and minimal cmd below. reproduces on dedicated pool with batch_size=4, seq=1536.

```
# run repro
python infra/bench/run.py --model llama-13b --device cuda:0 --batch 4 --seq 1536 --profile
```

Trace shows we pick kernel variant `matmul_tile_32x64_v2` on newer arch but then fall back to generic for attention because of register pressure. snippet from runtime trace: `choose_kernel(attn, arch=sm_80, heur=seqlen_1536) -> tile32_v2 (selected) -> fallback: generic_attn`

rui: perf-bot posted a flamegraph to the thread: https://ci.redwood/pf/1771234567/flame.html (perf-bot)

perf-bot: automated-profile: peak_reg_use=72, reg_spill=1.9x, smem_bytes=48k, occupancy=0.42, compute_eff=61%

sasha: looks like register pressure goes up when we use 32x64 tiles at seqlen>1024. we should test a 16x128 path that trades some smem for fewer regs. also check warp specialization: fewer warps per block might increase occupancy.

anita: can we try a runtime tweak that selects kernel by (arch, seq_bucket, batch_bucket) instead of current (arch, model_size) policy? seq_bucket = [<=512, 513-1024, >1024] would avoid picking the wrong tile for long sequences.

james: +1. quick A/B: add a lightweight cost model: cost = alpha*reg_spill + beta*(1-occupancy) + gamma*smem_usage. alpha/beta/gamma heuristics from perf-bot defaults. we can autotune the weights with offline runs.

sasha: I pushed a small kernel-profiles.json patch to my branch with 16x128 and 24x96 variants and a seq-aware selector. snippet:```json
{
  "variants": [
    {"name":"matmul_16x128","regs":60,"smem":64k,"seg":"long"},
    {"name":"matmul_24x96","regs":66,"smem":56k,"seg":"mid"}
  ],
  "selector":"seq_bucket"
}
```

rui: ran CI perf harness: 16x128 reduces reg_spill to 1.1x and latency down 11% on avg for seq=1536, but for seq=512 it regresses 4%. so selector needed. plot: https://ci.redwood/pf/1771234567/compare.png

anita: good. we should also guard against register-spill-induced L1 pressure. can we add a runtime probe: if reg_spill>1.5x within first 50 tokens, switch kernel mid-request? (hot path but might save long runs)

james: switching mid-request is hairy because of KV cache layout assumptions. but we can do mid-batch: detect after first token and route remaining micro-batches to alternate kernel. need to ensure KV offsets compatible.

sasha: KV-compatible kernels are possible if we keep same layout and only change tile dims. i'll draft compatibility doc. also note perf-bot flagged a bucketing edge-case: batch routing sometimes mixes seq=256 and seq=1536 in same batch due to our packer. that forces generic kernel. we should prefer binning by seq before packing.

rui: agreed. i'll add a change to the packer to prioritize seq-homogeneous batches (config flag: packer.seq_bin_priority=true). tests in CI.

perf-bot: follow-up-scan: runs queued for autotune sweep (variants:16x128,24x96,32x64) across sm_70/sm_80; estimated runtime 4h.

anita: next steps: (1) land seq-aware selector (2) adjust packer to prefer seq bins (3) autotune weights offline and commit best defaults (4) try mid-batch switch experiment behind feature flag.

james: I'll own seq-aware selector PR. assigning to @sasha for kernel compatibility doc. @rui please monitor autotune runs. thanks :thumbsup:

sasha: ack, will draft doc and post here. :rocket:

rui: will post CI runs + graphs once done.

james: filing a short follow-up incident note in #incidents if autotune run surfaces regressions.

anita: cool. low-risk rollout strategy -> canary on dedicated pool then global. :+1:
